_doc: Validation benchmark: past collapses with published cause findings. 'photos' = what published photographs of the debris show (scenario A); 'record' = public record available within about a week of the event, before any inquiry (scenario B). 'truth' = inquiry or investigation finding per network root: primary | contributing | ruled_out (omitted = not established). 'tier' grades the finding: official (statutory inquiry/court/coroner), professional (engineering-body or federal-agency investigation), interim (investigation not final), expert (expert opinion only). Observations were encoded from published photograph descriptions and widely circulated imagery by an assessor who knew the outcomes (NOT blind); see README section 'Validation'. Items not present in the library version under test are reported as unencoded and ignored.

rana_plaza_2013.name: Rana Plaza, Savar, Bangladesh

photos.basis: Aerial and street photos: floors stacked flat, rear section partly standing
No rotation of the mass; debris within the plot and road
Rescue tunnels into voids; survivors recovered up to 17 days later
Top floor under construction at the time

record.basis: Cracks in walls and pillars reported and building briefly closed the day before
Officials stated within days that upper floors were added without permission
Garment factories with heavy machinery and generators in a building designed as a shopping mall

rana_plaza_2013.finding: Inquiry (Mainuddin Ahmed committee): illegal extra floors, very poor cement mix and steel, part built on a filled pond, heavy machinery and generator vibration; cracks ignored.

sampoong_1995.name: Sampoong Department Store, Seoul, South Korea

photos.basis: South wing pancaked into the basements; north wing left standing
Vertical collapse, no overturning
Survivors recovered after 11 to 17 days

record.basis: Cracks and sagging in the 5th-floor ceiling reported hours before; store not evacuated

sampoong_1995.finding: Punching shear at column 5E; columns thinned and widely spaced; columns cut for escalators; 5th-floor change of use (heavy ondol floor) and 45 t of rooftop AC units dragged over the failed column.

harbour_cay_1981.name: Harbour Cay Condominium, Cocoa Beach, Florida, USA

photos.basis: All floors pancaked within the footprint
No rotation of the mass
Shores, reshores and formwork throughout the debris

record.basis: Collapsed while the roof slab was being concreted

harbour_cay_1981.finding: NBS (BSS 145): punching-shear capacity of the 5th-floor flat slab insufficient for construction loads; no punching check in design; slab thin and top steel set too high.

lotus_riverside_2009.name: Lotus Riverside Block 7, Shanghai, China

photos.basis: Building toppled intact onto its side
Open garage excavation on one side, soil stockpile on the other
Row of snapped precast piles exposed under the toppled raft

lotus_riverside_2009.finding: Officials: construction-procedure error. A 4.6 m excavation on one side and a 10 m soil stockpile on the other pushed the pile foundation sideways. Design, survey and materials not at fault.

ronan_point_1968.name: Ronan Point, Newham, London, UK

photos.basis: Tower standing; one corner bay missing from floor 18 to the podium
Load-bearing flank-wall panels missing at the initiating floor; partial, bay-wide collapse only

record.basis: Gas explosion in an 18th-floor flat reported immediately

ronan_point_1968.finding: Griffiths tribunal: town-gas explosion blew out load-bearing panels; progressive collapse of the corner was inherent in the large-panel design, not workmanship.

ikoyi_2021.name: Gerrard Road 21-storey tower, Ikoyi, Lagos, Nigeria

photos.basis: Floors stacked within the footprint
No overturning
Under construction; props and formwork in the debris
Survivors recovered from voids

record.basis: Reported within days: approval for 15 storeys, 21 built

ikoyi_2021.finding: Lagos panel: erosion of professional ethics and due diligence; NIStructE: design revised from 6 to 12, 15 then 21 storeys by several firms; ground-floor column failure, foundation not the root cause.

scoan_2014.name: Synagogue Church of All Nations guesthouse, Ikotun, Lagos, Nigeria

photos.basis: Floors stacked flat in the footprint
No overturning
Additional floors under construction on top at the time

record.basis: No planning approval; extra floors being added (reported at the time)

scoan_2014.finding: Coroner (2015): structural failure from design and detailing errors; extra floors added without approval to a building not designed for them; sabotage claim rejected.

ita_faji_2019.name: Ita-Faji school building, Lagos Island, Nigeria

photos.basis: Floors stacked flat between neighbours
No overturning
Children rescued from voids
Crumbling concrete visible in rescue photos (not verified by hand or test)

record.basis: Building marked as distressed and earmarked for demolition beforehand
School operating in a residential building

ita_faji_2019.finding: Federal committee (NBRRI): concrete strength below minimum design strength, weak mix, shallow foundation on low-bearing sandy soil, overloading from change of use to a school.

ronesans_2023.name: Ronesans Rezidans, Antakya, Hatay, Turkiye

photos.basis: Block toppled onto its side largely intact
Many surrounding buildings collapsed at the same time

record.basis: Mw 7.8 Kahramanmaras earthquake at the time of collapse

ronesans_2023.finding: Collapsed in the Mw 7.8 earthquake; experts cite a shallow raft without piles on soft alluvium. Court case ongoing; no published final technical report found.

hotel_new_world_1986.name: Hotel New World (Lian Yak Building), Singapore

photos.basis: Floors pancaked within the footprint
No overturning
17 people rescued from voids over several days

hotel_new_world_1986.finding: Commission of Inquiry (1987): structural design error (building self-weight underestimated) and poor construction; explosion and nearby MRT works ruled out.

melcom_2012.name: Melcom store, Achimota, Accra, Ghana

photos.basis: Floors stacked within the footprint
No overturning
Dozens rescued alive from voids

melcom_2012.finding: Ghana Institution of Engineers: very low concrete strength, inadequate column reinforcement, extra 100 mm screed on each floor; soil not the cause.

surfside_2021.name: Champlain Towers South, Surfside, Florida, USA

photos.basis: Central and east sections pancaked; west section left standing
No overturning of the collapsed mass
Corroded reinforcement visible in garage and pool-deck debris photos

record.basis: 2018 engineer's report of major structural damage below the pool deck; water and cracking in the garage minutes before

surfside_2021.finding: NIST interim (Sept 2025): failure most likely began at a pool-deck slab-column connection; pool deck built with fewer and wider-spaced top bars than designed; long-term water damage. Final report pending.
